title: Stochastic backpressure hedger and kernel matchmaker to reduce tail spikes in continuous batching
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: production serving shows intermittent tail-latency spikes during mixed workload bursts. Existing admission control is deterministic and reacts to queue depth, which over/under-allocates slots when short lived bursts collide with long-running decodes. This ticket implements a stochastic backpressure "hedger" that reserves ephemeral capacity for quantified tail risk and a lightweight kernel matchmaker that picks attention kernels and quantization paths based on short fingerprints of the batch to reduce per-batch variance.
acceptance_criteria: Integrated hedger into admission pipeline without adding >1ms steady-state median latency
Tail P99 latency improvement of >= 15% on mixed short-and-long request trace compared to baseline (current master) under identical load
Kernel matchmaker selects kernel variant and quantization path for >90% of batches and falls back safely on selection failures
No increase in token cost beyond 5% for typical inference workloads
E2E unit and integration tests for hedger boundary conditions and matchmaker timeouts added to CI
technical_notes: Hedger design: maintain an EWMA-based short-term arrival rate and a quantile reserve buffer. When short-term variance exceeds threshold, deduct reserved slots that are only released after a short cool-down window to avoid oscillation.
Reserve sizing uses a 95th-percentile estimator from a sliding window (configurable 30s default). Reserve budget is tenant-aware and can be capped by tenant SLA tier.

Matchmaker: compute a compact fingerprint per prefill (sequence length histogram + first-token entropy + model-variant tag) and consult a local model-to-kernel policy table to pick (kernel-impl, attention-optim, quant-profile). Fall back to default kernel on miss or timeout.

Prefill/decode interplay: hedger flags high-variance prefill batches to prefer low-latency kernels even if slightly higher compute cost; for decode-heavy batches prioritize kernels with better KV-cache locality.
Instrumentation: add histograms for reserve usage, matchmaker hit/miss, decision latency, and per-kernel micro-latency. Expose via runtime metrics dashboard and per-route breakdowns in Console.
Safety: all decisions are advisory to admission controller; a safety cap prevents hedger from starving high-priority tenant slots. Kernel matchmaker has a 200us decision budget before defaulting.
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype hedger library in sandbox: EWMA + quantile reserve impl (2 days)
2) Implement matchmaker fingerprint and local policy table with experimental feature flag (3 days)
3) Integrate hedger into admission flow and wire metrics (2 days)
4) Add kernel matchmaker call at kernel-selection point with 200us timeout and fallback (3 days)
5) Run controlled perf experiments using mixed-trace load generator and compare to baseline (2 days)
6) Iterate on thresholds and tenant caps, add config knobs in console (2 days)
7) Add unit/integration tests and rollout behind canary with telemetry dashboards (3 days)
8) Post-deploy monitor and rollback plan for first 72h (on-call schedule + runbook)
progress_updates: 2025-02-15: Ticket opened. Problem validated against SLO incident from 2025-02-10 where P99 spiked to 2.1x baseline during multi-tenant burst.
2025-02-18: Spike repro harness created and baseline metrics collected. Observed that 30% of spikes correlate with heavy decode jobs followed by many short prefill requests.
2025-02-22: Prototype hedger implemented in sandbox; initial manual tests show reserve smooths admission at the cost of a ~3% median token throughput reduction.
2025-02-26: Kernel matchmaker prototype (fingerprint + policy table) returns selections within 120-170us in local testing. Added hit/miss counters.
2025-03-02: End-to-end staging run with 1h mixed trace: P99 reduced by 18% and P995 reduced by 24% compared to baseline. Memory and GPU utilization within expected ranges.
2025-03-05: Design review completed with PM and Runtime leads. Plan to roll behind feature-flaged canary and monitor per-tenant effects. Working on CI tests and runbook.
